subject: biology
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: In a fish gill, the counter-current flow of water and blood is efficient because:
options: Blood and water flow in the same direction, equalising oxygen quickly
A diffusion gradient for oxygen is maintained across the entire length of the lamella
It allows carbon dioxide to be reabsorbed into the blood
Water flows faster than blood, reversing the gradient
questions.explain: Counter-current flow keeps the oxygen concentration of water higher than that of blood along the whole gill lamella, maintaining a diffusion gradient throughout.

questions.q: Glucose is absorbed across the ileum epithelium into the blood by:
options: Active transport directly using ATP at the apical membrane
Facilitated diffusion at the apical membrane independent of sodium
Co-transport with sodium ions, the Na+ gradient being maintained by a sodium-potassium pump
Simple diffusion only, down its concentration gradient
questions.explain: Na+/glucose co-transporters move glucose against its gradient using the Na+ gradient set up by the Na+/K+ pump on the basal membrane.

questions.q: As an organism increases in size, why does it require a specialised exchange surface?
options: Volume increases more slowly than surface area
Its surface-area-to-volume ratio increases, slowing diffusion
Larger cells respire anaerobically and need no oxygen
Its surface-area-to-volume ratio decreases, so diffusion across the body surface cannot meet metabolic demand
questions.explain: As size increases, volume rises faster than surface area, so the SA:V ratio falls and the body surface alone cannot supply the cells.

questions.q: Which factor would DECREASE the rate of transpiration from a leaf?
options: A decrease in atmospheric humidity
An increase in atmospheric humidity
An increase in air movement (wind)
A rise in temperature
questions.explain: Higher humidity reduces the water-potential gradient between the leaf air spaces and the atmosphere, slowing diffusion of water vapour out.

questions.q: Compared with elastic recoil in expiration, why are the walls of arteries elastic?
options: To allow active contraction that pumps blood
To slow blood flow for absorption
To enable exchange of materials with tissues
To stretch under high pressure and recoil, smoothing out pressure surges and maintaining flow
questions.explain: Elastic tissue in artery walls stretches during systole and recoils during diastole, evening out pulsatile pressure and sustaining blood flow.

questions.q: Carbon dioxide is mostly transported in the blood as:
options: Carbaminohaemoglobin
Dissolved CO2 in the plasma
Carbonic acid in the plasma
Hydrogencarbonate ions formed in red blood cells
questions.explain: Most CO2 is converted by carbonic anhydrase in red cells to carbonic acid, which dissociates into hydrogencarbonate ions carried in the plasma.

questions.q: Insects limit water loss from their tracheal system mainly by:
options: Using haemoglobin to carry oxygen in the blood
Producing surfactant in the tracheoles
Closing the spiracles using valves and hairs
Increasing ventilation by abdominal pumping
questions.explain: Spiracles can be closed by valves, reducing the evaporative water loss that would otherwise occur from the moist tracheal lining.

questions.q: During ventricular systole, the atrioventricular valves close because:
options: The ventricles are relaxing and filling
Atrial pressure exceeds ventricular pressure
The semilunar valves are open
Ventricular pressure exceeds atrial pressure
questions.explain: As the ventricles contract their pressure rises above that of the atria, forcing the AV valves shut to prevent backflow.

questions.q: The very large surface area of the small intestine for absorption is produced by:
options: A thick muscular wall
Numerous goblet cells secreting mucus
Villi and microvilli on the epithelial cells
A dense capillary network in the submucosa only
questions.explain: Folded villi each covered in microvilli (the brush border) massively increase the absorptive surface area of the ileum.

questions.q: In the cohesion-tension theory of water transport, water moves up the xylem because:
options: Active transport pumps water from root to leaf
Osmosis pushes water from the leaves down to the roots
Transpiration creates tension, and cohesion between water molecules pulls a continuous column upward
Root pressure alone is sufficient in tall trees
questions.explain: Evaporation from leaves lowers pressure, and hydrogen-bonded cohesion lets a continuous water column be pulled up under tension.

questions.q: The Bohr effect describes how an increase in carbon dioxide (and fall in pH):
options: Increases the oxygen-carrying capacity of the blood
Shifts the oxygen dissociation curve to the right, so haemoglobin releases more oxygen at a given partial pressure
Shifts the oxygen dissociation curve to the left, increasing haemoglobin's affinity
Has no effect on oxygen affinity
questions.explain: Higher CO2 lowers haemoglobin's oxygen affinity, shifting the curve right so more oxygen is unloaded in respiring tissues.

questions.q: The semilunar (aortic and pulmonary) valves open when:
options: The ventricles relax during diastole
Atrial pressure exceeds ventricular pressure
Ventricular pressure exceeds the pressure in the aorta and pulmonary artery
The AV valves are also open
questions.explain: Once ventricular pressure rises above arterial pressure the semilunar valves open and blood is ejected.
